algorithm.title: From an action trace to a gap sum

steps.title: Record the trace
steps.detail: Write the selected arm A_t at every round t.

steps.title: Count each arm
steps.detail: N_a(T) counts how often arm a appears before horizon T.

steps.title: Attach its gap
steps.detail: Every occurrence of arm a contributes the same model gap Δ_a.

steps.title: Regroup the sum
steps.detail: Replace the sum over time by one gap-times-count term per arm.

source_theorem.label: Lemma 4.5 (regret decomposition)
source_theorem.fallback: Expected regret is the sum, over arms, of each gap times that arm's expected pull count.
source_theorem.plain: The standard stochastic-bandit decomposition converts control of suboptimal pull counts into expected regret.
source_theorem.relationship: BanditRLlib first proves the pathwise finite-trace identity. Algorithm chapters then integrate that bookkeeping identity under their own generated trajectory laws.

steps.title: Model conditional noise
steps.detail: State a conditional MGF or bounded-reward assumption on the generated history.

steps.title: Derive one tail bound
steps.detail: Convert the MGF bound into a deviation probability at a fixed index.

steps.title: Allocate confidence
steps.detail: Assign a finite, geometric, or telescoping share δ_i to every arm and time.

steps.title: Join the events
steps.detail: Use a union bound to obtain one good event consumed by an algorithm proof.

source_theorem.label: Corollary 5.5 (sub-Gaussian tail)
source_theorem.fallback: A centered sub-Gaussian variable has an exponentially small upper-tail probability.
source_theorem.plain: The fixed-index tail estimate is the mathematical atom from which finite and all-time confidence schedules are assembled.
source_theorem.relationship: The local library adds measure, kernel, filtration, conditional-law, finite-index, and countable-all-time adapters needed by generated bandit trajectories.

steps.title: Explore
steps.detail: Pull every arm m times, usually in round-robin order.

steps.title: Estimate
steps.detail: Compute each arm's empirical mean from its exploration samples.

steps.title: Commit
steps.detail: Choose an empirical maximizer using a documented tie rule.

steps.title: Exploit
steps.detail: Pull that chosen arm for every remaining round.

source_theorem.label: Theorem 6.1 (ETC regret bound)
source_theorem.fallback: ETC regret is bounded by the exploration cost plus the remaining horizon times exponentially small wrong-commit probabilities.
source_theorem.plain: The theorem exposes the central ETC tradeoff: more exploration costs regret now but reduces the probability of committing to a wrong arm.
source_theorem.relationship: The local canonical route constructs a measurable generated ETC law and states explicit tie semantics before deriving bounded and sub-Gaussian expected-regret endpoints.

steps.title: Initialize
steps.detail: Pull every arm so that each empirical mean and count is defined.

steps.title: Score every arm
steps.detail: Add a confidence bonus to the arm's empirical mean; less data means a wider bonus.

steps.title: Choose optimistically
steps.detail: Pull an arm with maximal upper-confidence score.

steps.title: Update and repeat
steps.detail: Update that arm's count and empirical mean, then recompute scores next round.

steps.title: Read the proof
steps.detail: On the good event, choosing a suboptimal arm forces its count to still be small; sum gap times count to obtain regret.

source_theorem.label: Theorem 7.2 (finite-time UCB regret)
source_theorem.fallback: The textbook UCB policy has a finite-time regret bound with a leading square-root term in horizon, arm count, and log horizon.
source_theorem.plain: Confidence validity implies a suboptimal arm can be selected only while its sample count is small enough to keep its bonus competitive.
source_theorem.relationship: BanditRLlib's ordinary-UCB route uses an explicit generated trajectory and confidence schedule. Its exact hypotheses, constants, gap-sum form, and Tδ failure term are therefore not presented as a line-for-line formalization of Theorem 7.2; KL-UCB remains a separate extension.

companion.title: Improved Algorithms for Linear Stochastic Bandits
companion.authors: Yasin Abbasi-Yadkori, Dávid Pál, and Csaba Szepesvári

steps.title: Update geometry
steps.detail: Accumulate the regularized feature Gram matrix from past actions.

steps.title: Estimate
steps.detail: Compute the ridge least-squares parameter estimate.

steps.title: Build confidence
steps.detail: Place plausible parameters in an ellipsoid around the estimate.

steps.title: Act optimistically
steps.detail: Choose the action and plausible parameter pair with the largest predicted reward.

steps.title: Charge widths
steps.detail: Bound regret by confidence widths and use the elliptical-potential sum.

source_theorem.label: Abbasi-Yadkori–Pál–Szepesvári, Theorem 3
source_theorem.math: R_n=\widetilde O\!\left(d\sqrt n\right)\quad\text{under the theorem's bounded-feature and sub-Gaussian assumptions}.
source_theorem.fallback: OFUL achieves dimension times square-root-horizon regret, up to logarithmic factors, under the paper's stated assumptions.
source_theorem.plain: The paper combines a self-normalized confidence ellipsoid with optimism and an elliptical-potential argument.
source_theorem.relationship: The local finite-action scalar route compiles the confidence, optimistic policy, all-time, expected-consistency, and stopping-time interfaces under its own explicit contracts; consult the exact Lean statements for the narrower model.

steps.title: Condition
steps.detail: Form the posterior distribution of the unknown environment given observed history.

steps.title: Sample a model
steps.detail: Draw one plausible environment from that posterior.

steps.title: Optimize the sample
steps.detail: Choose an arm that is best in the sampled environment.

steps.title: Observe and update
steps.detail: Record the reward and condition the posterior on the enlarged history.

source_theorem.label: Theorem 36.1 (Bayesian regret of Thompson sampling)
source_theorem.math: BR_n\le C\sqrt{kn\log n}\quad\text{for the theorem's Bayesian finite-armed model and universal }C.
source_theorem.fallback: In the stated Bayesian finite-armed setting, Thompson sampling has square-root-horizon Bayesian regret up to a logarithmic factor.
source_theorem.plain: Probability matching turns posterior uncertainty about the best arm into an exploration policy.
source_theorem.relationship: BanditRLlib constructs a canonical posterior/kernel and generated stationary latent-arm-stream process. Its compiled terminal has explicit bounded-reward and variance terms and is not a blanket frequentist guarantee for all Thompson variants.

steps.title: Turn weights into probabilities
steps.detail: Normalize positive arm weights, with the prescribed exploration or support rule.

steps.title: Sample an arm
steps.detail: Draw the current action from that probability vector.

steps.title: Estimate all losses
steps.detail: Use the observed loss divided by its sampling probability for the selected arm; use zero for the others.

steps.title: Update exponentially
steps.detail: Downweight arms according to their estimated cumulative losses.

steps.title: Separate guarantees
steps.detail: Expected, fixed-horizon tail, all-time, and sparse-loss results use distinct concentration interfaces.

source_theorem.label: Theorem 11.2 (EXP3 expected regret)
source_theorem.fallback: With the textbook learning rate, EXP3 has expected adversarial regret at most the square root of two times horizon, arm count, and log arm count.
source_theorem.plain: Importance weighting makes the bandit observation unbiased, while exponential weights controls the resulting estimated-loss regret.
source_theorem.relationship: The local generated predictable process uses its own tuning constants and also compiles separate fixed-horizon, all-time, realized-regret, and sparse-loss extensions.

companion.title: Tsallis-INF: An Optimal Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits

steps.title: Estimate bandit losses
steps.detail: Construct an importance-weighted or reduced-variance estimate from the selected arm.

steps.title: Accumulate the estimate
steps.detail: Add the new estimate to the running loss vector.

steps.title: Regularize with half-Tsallis entropy
steps.detail: Choose the next distribution by minimizing estimated loss plus the scheduled Tsallis potential.

steps.title: Sample and adapt
steps.detail: Draw the next arm and update the learning-rate schedule; specialized theorems then add self-bounding, corruption, drift, or restart assumptions.

source_theorem.label: Zimmert–Seldin, Theorem 1 (adversarial regime)
source_theorem.fallback: The source theorem gives explicit adversarial square-root regret bounds for importance-weighted and reduced-variance Tsallis-INF variants.
source_theorem.plain: The half-Tsallis regularizer is designed to retain adversarial robustness while adapting sharply to stochastic self-bounding structure.
source_theorem.relationship: BanditRLlib proves a scheduled half-Tsallis route and several IID, corrupted, drifting, and oracle-restart consumers. These are source-aligned local theorems, not a claim that every sharp paper regime has been reproduced verbatim.

companion.title: Minimax Regret Bounds for Reinforcement Learning
companion.authors: Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, Ian Osband, and Rémi Munos

steps.title: Count strict prefixes
steps.detail: Before episode k, aggregate visits and next-state transitions from episodes strictly earlier than k.

steps.title: Estimate transitions
steps.detail: Normalize transition counts at each state-action pair, with an explicit zero-count convention.

steps.title: Plan backward optimistically
steps.detail: Add a Hoeffding bonus, clip against the horizon and previous Q table, and run backward dynamic programming.

steps.title: Execute the greedy policy
steps.detail: Generate the next episode with the measurable greedy policy from that recurrent table.

steps.title: Assemble regret
steps.detail: Combine confidence and optimism with charge, Bellman-innovation, and low-count bounds on the same process.

source_theorem.label: Azar–Osband–Munos, Theorem 1 (UCBVI-CH)
source_theorem.fallback: With high probability, UCBVI-CH regret is bounded by a 20-times square-root leading term plus the explicit 250-times lower-order term.
source_theorem.plain: The UCBVI-CH analysis couples empirical-transition concentration, backward optimism, cumulative bonuses, and a martingale innovation term.
source_theorem.relationship: The compiled local endpoint is deliberately narrow: finite horizon, known deterministic rewards, the same recurrent generated process, strict-prefix counts, policy-value pseudo-regret, the frozen 20/250 high-probability bound, and an expected consumer with an additional KHδ failure term.

steps.title: Initialize θ
steps.detail: Set θₖ,₁ = 0; the initial action law is uniform.

steps.title: Softmax law
steps.detail: Set pₖ,ₜ proportional to exp(θₖ,ₜ) over the finite arms.

steps.title: Sample reward
steps.detail: Draw Aₜ from pₜ and observe the selected arm's reward rₜ.

steps.title: Update θ
steps.detail: Add η rₜ(1{Aₜ = k} − pₖ,ₜ) to every coordinate.

steps.title: Split regret
steps.detail: Expected gap increments plus failure mass yield the finite-horizon bound.

source_theorem.label: Definitions 3.1–3.3 and Lemmas 3.1–3.4 (succinct-support geometry)
source_theorem.math: \(Q(\sum_i a_i E_i)=\max_i |a_i|,\qquad R(\sum_i a_i E_i)=\sum_i |a_i|,\qquad X\text{ s-succinct and strictly z-succinct}\Rightarrow z\le s.\)
source_theorem.fallback: On a succinct support, Q is the largest absolute coefficient and R is the sum of the absolute coefficients. For the same vector, a strict succinct representation uses no more atoms than any succinct representation.
source_theorem.plain: The source defines its atom set, succinct-support correlation contract, Q/R pair, and finite succinct representations. Its first four lemmas identify the coefficient norms and prove strict representation-size minimality and uniqueness for a fixed vector.
source_theorem.relationship: BanditRLlib compiles 54 declarations for Definitions 3.1–3.3 and Lemmas 3.1–3.4, including a finite-Bessel proof of strict representation-size minimality for the same vector, and separately diagnoses a global R boundedness obligation. The global Lemmas 3.5–3.6, Assumption 3.7, Theorem 3.8, and every regret endpoint remain outside the compiled slice.

source_theorems.label: Theorem 1 (two-arm SGB regret upper bound)
source_theorems.fallback: For a two-arm bounded-reward instance, Theorem 1 gives an explicit logarithmic-in-horizon regret term plus a finite failure-regret term whenever the learning rate satisfies η Cη < Δ.
source_theorems.plain: The source theorem combines a forward-potential logarithmic bound with a telescoping control of squared failure probability for the same fixed-IID two-arm SGB trajectory.
source_theorems.relationship: BanditRLlib compiles this exact Theorem-1 endpoint for the actual sampled pseudo-regret of bounded two-arm fixed-IID laws, specialized through a Unit Dirac environment prior. A separate eight-declaration Appendix-E gate checks finite scalar contracts used in Theorem 4, but does not prove that theorem. The Theorem-1 contract keeps 0 < Delta < 1, eta > 0, eta C_eta < Delta, exact arm means, and T = tailHorizon + 1 explicit. A later 23-declaration Corollary-1 companion compiles as a direct consumer; it is not evidence for Theorem 2.

source_theorems.label: Corollary 1 (horizon-indexed two-arm SGB rate)
source_theorems.fallback: For every source horizon T, choose one fixed learning rate equal to the square root of log T divided by T; the resulting two-arm regret is at most a constant times the square root of T log T.
source_theorems.plain: Corollary 1 balances the already proved small-learning-rate Theorem-1 branch against the pathwise Delta-times-T bound. It describes a horizon-indexed family of fixed-rate policies, not one policy whose rate changes during a run.
source_theorems.relationship: Twenty-three new declarations compile an explicit finite companion on the generated zero-initialized two-arm fixed-IID trajectory with a Unit Dirac environment prior. For T >= 2 and 0 < Delta < 1, twoArmFixedIIDDirac_corollaryOne bounds expected sampled pseudo-regret by (2 + 1/log 2 + 2 exp 2) sqrt(T log T). The arm reward laws remain bounded fixed-IID laws; the Dirac measure is the prior on the singleton environment, not a claim that rewards are Dirac or Rademacher. This is a direct Theorem-1 consumer and is not independent Theorem-2 evidence.

source_theorems.label: Theorem 2 (two-arm SGB phase transition)
source_theorems.pages: physical PDF p. 6; Appendix C pp. 31–40
source_theorems.fallback: Above the two-arm critical learning rate, Theorem 2 gives a polynomial-in-horizon regret lower bound up to logarithmic factors, with the exponent reduced by an arbitrary positive epsilon.
source_theorems.plain: Appendix C reindexes the generated process by optimal-arm pull count, constructs a low-probability phase for that arm, and turns a no-return event into a long starvation interval and polynomial regret.
source_theorems.relationship: The exact K = 2 target remains blocked. Eighteen declarations compile a deterministic source-shaped fixed-cutoff consumer: twoArmFixedIIDStepOneStarvationEvent_charge_mul_probability_le_integral proves the exact Delta(T-n) sampled-regret charge and its probability-weighted expectation lower bound. A 24-declaration formalization-infrastructure layer defines the zero-based optimal-arm nth-pull time in WithTop Nat, proves stopping-time/measurability and exact finite count/action semantics, and identifies measurable stopped reward and post-pull probability values. Seven declarations prove the fixed-arm finite latent-prefix product law and finite nth-pull coordinate readout. Eight deferred-decisions declarations prove the finite stream-box product law, visible-prefix kernel-law locality, a Markov visible-prefix kernel, and the exact joint finite stream-box/visible-prefix mixture. A 13-declaration interface scaffold proves mixed-coupling next-action factorization and pathwise selected-coordinate support and states the branch-locality contract. The new 28-declaration producer proves safe-fiber restricted semidirect-product transport, the count-cap base/successor induction, that exact branch-locality contract, and an unconditional finite/sub-Markov branchwise product law. These target branches are not yet aggregated into selected-reward freshness, and the mixture's visible marginal is not yet identified with the native fixed-IID prefix. Selected-reward IID, the native visible law, and composition with the fixed-cutoff consumer remain unproved. Neither totalized nor occurrence-conditioned stopped rewards are claimed IID. The stopped-prefix future-cylinder law, conditional no-return probability at least one half, the Rademacher/binomial ballot phase, asymptotic assembly, and the frozen Theorem-2 terminal remain uncompiled.

source_theorems.label: Theorem 4 / Appendix E source-contract window
source_theorems.math: \[\begin{gathered}\eta C_\eta < \frac{2\Delta}{K+2},\\ 2\Delta-\eta C_\eta(K+2)>0,\\ 0<p',\quad c<\tfrac12,\\ P(B)\ge p',\\ P(B\cap S)\ge(1-2c)P(B),\\ P(B\cap S)\le P(S),\\ \Longrightarrow P(S)\ge p'(1-2c)>0.\end{gathered}\]
source_theorems.fallback: The printed tuning yields a positive drift margin. For positive p-prime and c below one half, explicit buffer and conditional-survival premises make the finite survival mass at least the positive quantity p-prime times one minus two c.
source_theorems.plain: This is the finite contract consumed by the Appendix-E transient-phase argument, not the statement of Theorem 4 itself.
source_theorems.relationship: Eight Lean declarations compile the positive margin, audited finite event composition, and finite geometric phase envelope. They expose an unresolved Step-4 conditioning/direction mismatch while leaving the general-K generated process, uniform buffer/survival producer, stopped supermartingale/Doob route, and Theorem 4 uncompiled.
